name: Trimethyl orthoformate
description: Trimethyl orthoformate ( CAS 149-73-5 ), commonly abbreviated as TMOF and also known as methyl orthoformate, is a reactive orthoacid ester used as a protecting group reagent and synthetic building block. It serves as a vital solvent across pharmaceutical and specialty chemical manufacturing. Its primary commercial role is enabling controlled reactions in sensitive synthesis environments where conventional reagents would cause unwanted side reactions. In pharmaceutical synthesis, TMOF acts as a methoxymethylating agent and carbonyl-protecting reagent. This enables the construction of complex active pharmaceutical ingredient intermediates with high selectivity during the manufacturing process. Agrochemical and fine chemical producers use it as a formylation reagent to introduce formate functionality into target molecules under mild conditions. This versatility makes it a staple in modern industrial chemistry. In flavor and fragrance manufacturing, it functions as a precursor to orthoester-based aroma compounds. It also serves as a stabilizing carrier solvent for sensitive fragrance ingredients that require specific chemical environments. Biotechnology applications include its use as a low-water solvent medium for enzymatic reactions. This is particularly useful where aqueous conditions would compromise yield or selectivity in delicate biological processes. The product is supplied as a colorless liquid in standard packaging ranging from small laboratory quantities to bulk drum shipments. Technical and synthesis-grade specifications are the most commonly available for industrial use. Purity levels are typically at 98% or higher for pharmaceutical and fine chemical applications.
